rule: A RATCHET. Every list here is a baseline of what existed when it was written, and it may only shrink. A new entry fails the build; a retired entry is dropped automatically, because removing one can only make the check stricter. Adding an entry is a hand edit with a reason.

docs/ADR-002-showdown-is-the-authority.m.reason: AN ADR IS A DATED DECISION, NOT A LIVING DOCUMENT. It records that Showdown is the authority and MEDICHAM the runtime, decided and ACCEPTED at 3.50.0. Nothing in 3.51.0 revisits that decision — GARY, DUSK and the search reordering all sit downstream of it and none of them changes which engine is authoritative. Bumping the stamp would assert a review that did not happen. Unpin only when the decision itself is amended or superseded.

docs/ADR-003-exploitability-is-the-headl.reason: AN ADR IS A DATED DECISION, NOT A LIVING DOCUMENT — the same reason ADR-002 is pinned one entry up. It records that exploitability is the headline, accepted at 3.71.0. ROADMAP #92 is an engine-correctness pass and changes nothing this decision rests on.

docs/ARCHITECTURE-NOTES.md.reason: OWN VERSION LINE — companion notes to ARCHITECTURE.md and stamped on its scheme, not the project one.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.reason: OWN VERSION LINE — an architecture document, versioned independently of the model releases.

docs/CLICK-CENSORING-FIX.md.reason: SPEC FOR A SHIPPED RELEASE - it is the written specification of the 3.42.0 click-censoring work, and its content is current FOR that release. Bumping its header at every later release would assert it had been revisited when it had not.

docs/ENGINE-COVERAGE-PLAN.md.reason: DEBT — carries the project version and sits one release behind (3.40.0 vs 3.41.0); Layer 0 landed in 3.41.0, so the plan describes work that has since moved.

docs/GAME-DIFFERENTIAL-DESIGN.md.reason: THE DESIGN OF AN INSTRUMENT, current for the instrument as it stands. ROADMAP #92 changed the SIMULATOR, not the differential harness, and the one thing it touches in this document was already true: the header records that moveHit does not run ModifyMove/spreadHit/willCrit, which is the boundary tests/test-damage-stages.js states for itself and stages by hand.

docs/GLOSSARY.md.reason: A VOCABULARY, not a result. ROADMAP #92 introduced no new term — "stage", "chain" and "modifier" are Showdown's own words and already appear here through docs/TAGS.md. It moves when a term is added or redefined, not when the engine gets more correct.

note_unversioned: These documents carry no version header, so nothing can say whether they are current. They are EXEMPT FROM RULE 1 ONLY - they are still scanned by the retracted-number rules. The list may only shrink: give a document a version header matching the CHANGELOG and it leaves this list and joins the figure scans.
note_archive: docs/archive/ files that do NOT declare a SUPERSEDED replacement. Grandfathering here only stops the SUPERSEDED-header rule failing; it grants NO exemption from the content scans, and the sixteen files archived on 2026-08-05 were deliberately left undeclared for exactly that reason. Moving a file into docs/archive/ must not convert a caught retracted figure into an uncaught one, so these carry a provenance header (what it claimed / when / what replaced it / what in it is retracted) and STAY in rules 1, 1b and 3b. Use the SUPERSEDED form only for a document whose content is wholly reproduced elsewhere. docs/archive/INDEX.md is GENERATED by build/build_archive_index.js and is the index over this directory, not an archived document.
note_known: What rule 3 found on 2026-08-05. Every entry is a REPORTED DEFECT, not an approval. The ratchet exists so the list cannot grow while these are worked through; it is not a statement that any of them is acceptable. Fixing a document retires its entry automatically on the next run.
note_unversioned_running_notes: HAND EDIT, 2026-09-06. docs/RUNNING-NOTES.md carries NO version header ON PURPOSE and is exempt from rule 1 only. Will, 2026-09-06: "we can update the documents every major release and just keep a running notes page in between change the documentation rules". A version header is a document CLAIMING TO BE CURRENT AS OF A VERSION; this file is a LOG of every change since the last major, so no single version describes it and a header would be an assertion nobody could check. Its currency is checked instead by clause 5, which is stricter than a header: git must show no commit moving code or a document since this file last moved, and the backlog it owes the next major must stay under OWED_CAP. It is NOT exempt from the content rules - rules 1, 1b, 3b(a) and 3b(b) all scan it, and tests/test-docs-current.js adds it to the citation scan by name. It is out of the 3b(c) census because that clause is a per-document count that may only fall and this file is append-only, so including it would build a gate guaranteed to go red for recording work faithfully.
